input.quote: c. the amount of any other actual direct damages, up to the greater of $100,000 or the charges paid by Customer to IBM for the Services in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the accrual of the first claim related to the Services.
input.rationale: Caps are mutual and use a 12-month fee basis (Sections 9.1(c)/9.2(c)), and the consequential-damages waiver in Section 10 is mutual with a carve-out for Customer's payment obligations, so the structure meets the fallback shape. However, three points deviate from our preferred position: (i) the monetary floor is only $100,000 (vs. USD 1,000,000) and is measured on charges "paid" rather than "paid or payable"; (ii) there are no carve-outs from the cap for breach of confidentiality/data protection and security obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or infringement of the other party's IP (only indemnity payments and bodily injury/property damage sit outside the capped bucket); and (iii) Section 9.1(c)(2) excludes IBM's liability entirely for loss of or damage to Customer's records or data, which is a one-sided exclusion of our principal risk in a hosting arrangement. The redline raises the floor to $1,000,000 on both sides, adds "or payable", adds a mutual Excluded Claims provision, and confirms the data-loss exclusion does not cover IBM's own security or confidentiality breaches.

proposal.summary: Raise mutual liability cap floor to $1,000,000 on "paid or payable" charges, add mutual uncapped carve-outs (confidentiality/data security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), and limit the blanket data-loss exclusion.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is a mutual cap at the greater of USD 1,000,000 and 12 months' charges paid or payable, so we have raised the floor and aligned the basis on both sides. We have also confirmed that indemnities, confidentiality/data-security breaches, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, and that IBM's blanket exclusion for loss of Customer records or data cannot cover its own security or confidentiality failures in a hosting arrangement; a 12-month fee cap with at least the indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct carve-outs is our fallback.

ops.newText: 2. loss of, or damage to, Customer's or any other entity's records or data, except to the extent arising out of IBM's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations.

ops.text: Excluded Claims. The limitations and exclusions of liability in Sections 9.1 and 9.2 do not apply to: (a) a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations; (b) a party's indemnification obligations under Section 8; (c) a party's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud; (d) a party's infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights; or (e) Customer's obligation to pay charges due under this Agreement, which will not be treated as damages for purposes of this Section 9.
